'''Note:''' This page lists '''sourced''' Players Committee (PC) Advocate / Player Advocate names and roles from dated primary or archived pages. It does '''not''' invent biographies, exact term dates, or legal names behind forum handles. Uncertain spans are labeled. Parent narrative: [[History of the Players Committee]].

The [[Players Committee]] is an organization of '''[[Advocate|Advocates]]''' (also called Player Advocates / the Advocate Council on early PC sites): volunteer leaders named by Decipher and later by the PC to support organized play, rules, design, tournaments, and community liaison after Decipher's print end-of-life. The current '''Lead Advocate''' (Head Advocate) is [[Scott Lingrell]]; his [[GEMP]] handle is '''advocate'''.

'''Origin (Decipher call for volunteers):''' Decipher's Star Wars Announcement page invited players to '''volunteer for the players' committee''' (contact listed on that page) alongside Decipher and Lucas Licensing contacts, and linked the '''01.25.02''' "The Star Wars Players' Committee" announcement.<ref name="deciphercall">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020601152726/http://decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], decipher.com (Wayback, 1 June 2002)</ref> The Player Advocates / Players' Committee structure therefore begins in Decipher's public call for volunteers and the January 2002 committee announcement&mdash;not as an independent later invention. Details of that handoff also appear on [[History of the Players Committee]].

== First team (Decipher announcement, 25 January 2002) ==

Warren Holland (Chairman &amp; CEO, Decipher), in a letter dated '''25 January 2002''' on Decipher's "The Star Wars Players' Committee" page, announced the '''first team of Star Wars Player Advocates''' selected from volunteer emails after the license announcement. The page states Advocates would meet Decipher in Norfolk the following week, receive the volunteer email list, work with Game Players Network on communications, handle prize shipping after '''30 April 2002''', and teased a forthcoming virtual-card pool.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002; letter dated 25 January 2002)</ref>

== Remaining mid-era gap (after Aug 2008 into early starwarsccg.org) ==

Public '''named''' Advocate Council lists are still thin between this '''~August 2008''' Encyclopedia Volunteer snapshot and the ~October 2014 starwarsccg.org About handles block in the sources used here. Contemporary '''about''' / "Who We Are" pages from 2008–2010 describe the PC historically but often omit a named Advocate roster in the archived HTML checked for this page.<ref name="about2008">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080925005351/http://www.swccgpc.com/about/ Who We Are / about], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 25 September 2008)</ref><ref name="swcabout2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706043114/http://www.starwarsccg.org/about/ about], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 6 July 2009)</ref>

'''Do not''' silently equate 2006 Content pid=3 roles with 2008 Encyclopedia titles (several role labels and people change across those captures).

== Gaps ==

* Exact start/end dates for most Advocate terms beyond the dated captures above.
* Named roster coverage after the ~August 2008 Encyclopedia Volunteer snapshot into ~2014 About handles remains thin in checked IA samples (about pages often omit names).
* Legal names behind remaining 2014 forum handles '''not''' proven by the org charts cited here: raith, LukesBionicHand. (Aug 2008 Encyclopedia Volunteer Information lists Mike Tomashewski as Shewski, Jim Colson as ShadowLeader, and Doug Taylor as DougRed4—those three handles are evidenced for 2008, not automatically for 2014 continuity.)
* Continuity of 2014 roles into 2021/2024 for handles that changed (e.g. Design: Shewski on 2014 About vs [[Chris Kelly]] / chriskelly on org charts)&mdash;do not invent overlap without a dated primary.
* Whether every Decipher "support" label maps 1:1 onto later "Advocate" titles (roles evolved; cite each era's own wording).
* Person stubs not yet created for every mid-era name (Colson, Robinette, Velasco, Carr, Brownell, Kolnik, and unresolved 2014 handles).
